seatMission: Integrate D01-D05 and optimize strategic coherence, capital and transferability.
seatResponsibilities: Integrate reconciled Director outputs D01-D05 within Strategy and Capital; resolve priorities and trade-offs without erasing governance conditions, dissent, contradictions, or invalidation conditions.

criterionDimensions.name: Governed VP opinion and upward handoff

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical Vice President mission, quality focus, governed-input rules, Director portfolio, upward governance requirements and explicit prohibitions are decomposed into 10 executive integration dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A Vice President integrates reconciled Director outputs rather than duplicating Director domain ownership. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I integrate D01-D05 only after required Council III reconciliation.
I verify that D01-D05 address the same decision, entity, scope, and time horizon before synthesis.
I preserve conditions attached to reconciled Director outputs.
I keep evidence identifiers, confidence, contradictions, and decisions required visible through integration.
I distinguish a missing Director input from an unfavorable Director conclusion.
I identify when a reconciled input has become stale enough to require refresh.
I request targeted clarification when Director outputs are not comparable enough for a responsible trade-off.
I avoid reopening settled domain analysis merely because I prefer another strategic outcome.
I reject synthesis when material input provenance or governance state is missing.
I treat governed input readiness as a prerequisite to executive integration.
I test whether the D02 strategy actually solves the problem and decision framed by D01.
I preserve root-cause uncertainty when strategic choices depend on unproven hypotheses.
I compare strategic options against explicit decision criteria rather than narrative attractiveness.
I identify strategies that optimize symptoms while leaving material causes untouched.
I require strategic choices to state what the enterprise will not pursue.
I connect advantage claims to the proof requirements defined for the decision.
I distinguish enterprise priorities from a list of simultaneously desirable initiatives.
I challenge strategies whose success conditions conflict with decision constraints.
I preserve alternative hypotheses when evidence does not justify one strategic story.
I make the logic from problem framing to strategic choice reconstructable.
I test whether strategy coheres with how the business creates, delivers, and captures value.
I surface conflicts between growth ambition and the economics of the current business model.
I preserve purpose constraints when profitable options materially violate stated institutional purpose.
I distinguish stakeholder value creation from shifting burden to another stakeholder.
I test whether priorities reinforce or erode capabilities on which the business model depends.
I identify when the business model must change before the strategy can plausibly succeed.
I separate purpose claims from evidence that operating and economic choices honor them.
I compare strategic alternatives by economic integrity and purpose integrity.
I expose hidden subsidies or dependencies that make a business model appear stronger than it is.
I make business-model coherence explicit in the VP opinion rather than assumed.
I use behavioral market evidence to test whether strategic assumptions are reachable.
I distinguish total market narratives from the market the enterprise can credibly access.
I compare advantage claims against competitor behavior and customer alternatives.
I identify when customer evidence supports demand but not the proposed positioning.
I preserve disagreement between market evidence and internal strategic conviction.
I test whether chosen segments fit capabilities and economics assumed elsewhere.
I distinguish stated preference from observed behavior when prioritizing strategic bets.
I identify strategic dependence on market conditions outside management control.
I make competitive-response assumptions explicit when they materially affect the choice.
I reduce confidence when market evidence is sparse, stale, indirect, or non-comparable.
I compare capital uses by strategic contribution, cash demand, risk, timing, and reversibility.
I connect investment recommendations to the strategic choices they enable.
I distinguish valuation upside from cash survival when ranking capital-intensive initiatives.
I identify when acquisition or partnership economics conflict with strategic constraints.
I compare build, buy, partner, acquire, divest, and defer alternatives when material.
I preserve downside and sensitivity findings even when an investment case is strategically attractive.
I distinguish transaction readiness from the desirability of completing a transaction.
I test valuation assumptions against accepted market, business-model, and risk evidence.
I surface the opportunity cost of capital committed to one strategic path.
I avoid ranking capital choices solely by headline return when control or optionality differs.
I treat founder dependence as a strategic and valuation variable rather than a personal preference.
I identify priorities that increase transferability while preserving essential differentiation.
I distinguish growth that deepens key-person dependence from growth that builds institutional capability.
I evaluate whether strategic options make the business easier or harder to operate without the current owner.
I connect governance, documentation, recurring economics, and leadership depth to transferability.
I surface trade-offs between founder-led advantage today and enterprise independence tomorrow.
I preserve transfer optionality even when an exit is not the current objective.
I recognize transaction theses that depend on capabilities residing in one individual.
I include transferability implications in capital ranking when they are material.
I treat reduced founder dependence as value creation only when essential capability is preserved.
I preserve material contradictions across D01-D05 as named conflicts with traceable sources.
I distinguish true contradiction from differences in scope, definition, period, or scenario.
I avoid resolving Director disagreement by seniority, confidence tone, or verbosity.
I compare conflicting claims by evidence strength and decision consequence.
I retain minority Director positions when governance has not invalidated them.
I identify conflicts that require renewed Director work rather than VP arbitration.
I state when a VP trade-off is a management preference rather than an evidentiary resolution.
I keep invalidation conditions attached to strategic conclusions.
I avoid synthesis language that falsely implies consensus.
I escalate conflicts crossing legal, constitutional, or irreversible-action boundaries.
I rank strategic priorities using explicit enterprise criteria.
I sequence initiatives when one creates evidence or capability required by another.
I recommend abandonment when an option no longer clears its strategic or evidence threshold.
I distinguish deferred initiatives from rejected initiatives and state reconsideration conditions.
I protect scarce capital and management attention from low-leverage strategic work.
I compare priorities by value, urgency, dependency, risk, reversibility, and strategic fit.
I identify the smallest set of priorities sufficient to advance the chosen strategy.
I surface when another priority would materially dilute execution of higher-value commitments.
I preserve optionality when evidence is insufficient for irreversible concentration.
I make the opportunity cost of lower-ranked alternatives visible.
I calibrate the recommendation to uncertainty remaining after Director reconciliation.
I distinguish reversible experiments from commitments that constrain future strategic options.
I favor staged capital commitment when uncertainty can be reduced first.
I define decision checkpoints tied to evidence when appropriate.
I identify assumptions whose failure would invalidate the VP recommendation.
I separate risk acceptance within VP scope from risks requiring higher authority.
I escalate irreversible or materially sensitive actions instead of approving them by implication.
I preserve Council conditions as active constraints on the recommendation.
I state when coherence cannot be achieved without a Human Decision Owner trade-off.
I avoid using urgency to bypass required governance stages.
I produce a VP opinion stating direction, priorities, trade-offs, and unresolved conditions.
I show how D01-D05 materially contributed without reproducing five separate reports.
I preserve evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and dissent required for auditability.
I separate findings, interpretations, management trade-offs, and recommendations.
I state capital implications and transferability consequences of the recommended direction.
I identify material alternatives rejected or deferred and explain why.
I make required Strategist decisions explicit.
I compress for executive use without deleting material uncertainty.
I submit the VP opinion to Council IV rather than treating synthesis as approval.
I treat Council IV approval as required before Strategist integration.
